title.narrative: Dhaka Environmentally Sustainable Water Supply Project

description.narrative: The project will provide more reliable and improved security of water supply in Dhaka by developing a new surface water supply scheme for supply augmentation, which includes the development of a water intake at Meghna River, a raw water transmission pipeline, a water treatment plant (WTP) at Gandharbpur with capacity of 500 million liters per day (MLD), a treated water transmission pipeline to the existing water supply network, and distribution reinforcements. The project will also include distribution network improvements to reduce nonrevenue water (NRW); and will improve the quality of water supply services, including support to low-income communities.

description.narrative: More reliable and improved security of water supply and sanitation in Dhaka achieved

At least 10,000 women and 1,000 vulnerable people in LICs received improved sanitation services Progress/Status: Not due yet. Consultants (Individual & NGOs) are working. Civil works under 7 packages (lots) are in progress.
The physical progress of construction of 358 units/WASH blocks comprised of 615 nos. community toilets and 377 nos. bathing facility under 4 lots is 99%; while the physical progress of construction of 220 units/WASH blocks comprised of 332 nos. community toilets and 229 nos. bathing facility under other 3 lots is 85%. Data Source: DWASA surveys Actual value:
Water supply pressure of at least one bar at consumer end achieved Progress/Status: Not due yet. Data Source: DWASA surveys Actual value:

Dependence on groundwater in project areas reduced to 30% for sustainable water supply and greater resilience to climate change Progress/Status: Not due yet. Till date, dependence on groundwater reduced to 26% in Zone 5, and 7% in Zone 8. Data Source: DWASA surveys Actual value:

3 million people in zones 5, 6, 8, 9, and 10 received continuous water supply Progress/Status: Not due yet. All the major civil works contracts have been awarded and are under implementation. The new water supply system is expected to complete in Q2 2027. About 495.89 km pipeline under 16 district metered areas are completed. Data Source: DWASA surveys Actual value:
Nonrevenue water reduced to 15% or less in 16 district metered areas in zone 6 Progress/Status: Not due yet. Till date, nonrevenue water reduced to 5%. Data Source: DWASA surveys Actual value:

98% of water quality test results within DWASA distribution systems met country standards Progress/Status: Not due yet. Till date, 95% of water quality test results meet country standards. Data Source: Joint surveys of DWASA and Department of Environment Actual value:
